doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: One Day Forever and writing ballads for Shirley Horn and Art Farmer
summary: Golson says his two tracks with Shirley Horn on One Day Forever were memorable because she was his favorite singer, and Art Farmer his instrumental ballad ideal.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Let’s talk about that album. This was the latest album I was able to find: One Day Forever, where you have the two selections from Shirley on here, and then you have your other – actually, you’ve got Art Farmer on here.

No, I did two after that. But that to me was memorable because of her. She was my favorite singer. Whenever I wrote a ballad, I thought about two people, one vocally and one instrumentally. I thought of her vocally and Art Farmer instrumentally.
Whenever I wrote a ballad, I thought about those two people, because they were masters of the ballad.
